title: Continuous conormal injectivity on residue fibres of a geometrically regular affinoid quotient
statement:
Let $K$ be a field complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $r,s\geq0$ and let $A=K\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$ be the ring of series $\sum_
u a_
u x^
u$ such that for every $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many coefficients satisfy $|a_
u|\geq\epsilon$. Fix $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in A$, put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ and $C=A/I$, and assume that for every isometric embedding $K\hookrightarrow L$ into a complete real-valued nonarchimedean field the coefficient-extended quotient $L\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle/(f_{1,L},\ldots,f_{s,L})$ is regular Noetherian [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $\mathfrak n\subset A$ be any maximal ideal containing $I$; maximal means proper and maximal among proper ideals. Put $\kappa=A/\mathfrak n$, a field, and give $I/\mathfrak n I$ its quotient $\kappa$-vector space structure. For $g\in I$, let $[g]$ denote its class in this quotient. Then the $\kappa$-linear map
$$d_{\mathfrak n}: I/\mathfrak n I\longrightarrow\kappa^{\oplus r},\qquad [g]\longmapsto igl(\partial g/\partial x_i mod\mathfrak n igr)_{i=1}^r$$
is injective. Here partial derivatives are termwise continuous derivatives of the restricted series. The assertion includes $r=0$, $s=0$, and the zero quotient (in the latter case there is no such maximal ideal).

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.20--21, the continuous conormal criterion and the choice of independent defining equations at a maximal ideal; geometric regularity versus analytic smoothness for general complete nonarchimedean fields: Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1999__49_2_473_0.pdf, section 3.3, printed pp.509--512. Agent-formulated residue-fibre version; neither analytic source is archived locally (WANTED).

proof.text: Termwise differentiation preserves restrictedness: $|n|\leq1$ for every integer $n$ in a nonarchimedean field, so a differentiated coefficient has magnitude at most that of its originating coefficient. The finite coefficient formulas for Cauchy multiplication give Leibniz. If $h\in\mathfrak n I$, write $h=\sum a_jg_j$ with $a_j\in\mathfrak n$ and $g_j\in I\subseteq\mathfrak n$; then every $\partial h/\partial x_i$ lies in $\mathfrak n$. The same product formula shows $d(ag)\equiv a\,dg\pmod{\mathfrak n}$ for $g\in I$. Thus the displayed map is well defined and $\kappa$-linear.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof: the continuous differential on the conormal module; explicit coefficient verification by the agent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-tate-maximal-residue-evaluation] to $A$ and $\mathfrak n$. Set $L=\kappa=A/\mathfrak n$ with its finite-extension absolute value, and $a_i=x_i\bmod\mathfrak n$. Then $K\hookrightarrow L$ is isometric and $L$ is complete, including in the inseparable case. Set $B=L\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle$ and let $\varphi:A\to B$ extend coefficients. Evaluation $B\to L$ restricts on $A$ to the given quotient map. Its kernel $\mathfrak q$ therefore satisfies $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak n$ and contains $IB$.

source.place: Theorem 1.1.5(1), Exercise 1.1.4 and subsequent residue-evaluation discussion; finite residue extension reduction.

proof.text: By [lem-per-tate-finite-scalar-extension], $\varphi$ is flat. By [lem-per-tate-rational-local-coordinates], $R=B_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local, its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qR$, its residue field is $L$, and the derivative coordinates give $\theta:\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\simeq L^r$. Put $J=(IB)R\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The hypothesis of the item applied to this particular $L$ says $B/IB$ is regular Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], $R/J\simeq(B/IB)_{\mathfrak q/IB}$, which is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Theorem 1.1.5(1), Exercise 1.2.8(4); ordinary localization of the geometrically regular quotient.

proof.text: Use the affine assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-flat-base-change] first for the flat map $A\to B$, then for $B\to R$, flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. It gives $(I/I^2)\otimes_A B\simeq IB/(IB)^2$ and $(IB/(IB)^2)\otimes_B R\simeq J/J^2$, both carrying an equation to its image. Tensor these isomorphisms with the residue field $L$. Balancing pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $(I/I^2)\otimes_A L\simeq(J/J^2)\otimes_R L$. Since $A\to L$ has kernel $\mathfrak n$ and $R\to L$ has kernel $\mathfrak m$, these modules are $I/\mathfrak n I$ and $J/\mathfrak m J$: the maps are $[g]\otimes\lambda\mapsto[ag]$, for any lift $a$ of $\lambda$, with inverse $[g]\mapsto[g]\otimes1$ (and similarly over $R$). Lift independence follows from $\mathfrak n I$ or $\mathfrak m J$; $I^2\subseteq\mathfrak n I$ and $J^2\subseteq\mathfrak m J$. We obtain an $L$-linear isomorphism $\alpha:I/\mathfrak n I\simeq J/\mathfrak m J$, $[g]\mapsto[\varphi(g)/1]$. The scalar action on the source is the original $\kappa=L$ action, not a new tensor extension of that field.

source.place: Tag 0473, lemma-conormal-functorial-flat, affine proof; the residue quotient formulas are written out here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-independent-generators] to the regular local ring $R$, the ideal $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and its regular local quotient $R/J$. It supplies finitely many $u_1,\ldots,u_c\in J$ generating $J$ whose classes are linearly independent in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ over $L$.

The inclusion $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ induces $\beta:J/\mathfrak m J\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. If $z=\sum_{j=1}^c b_ju_j\in J$ represents a kernel element, then $0=[z]=\sum_j\bar b_j[u_j]$ in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. The independence obtained in Step 5 forces every $b_j\in\mathfrak m$, so $z\in\mathfrak m J$. Thus $\beta$ is injective. This argument also applies when $c=0$.

source.place: Tag 00NR independent generators; elementary linear combination argument from Step 5.

proof.text: For each $g\in I$, [lem-per-tate-rational-local-coordinates] gives $(\theta\beta\alpha)([g])=((\partial\varphi(g)/\partial x_i)(a))_i$. Coefficient extension commutes with termwise derivatives, and evaluation at $a$ restricts to reduction modulo $\mathfrak n$ by Step 2. Hence this vector is exactly $d_{\mathfrak n}([g])$. Thus $d_{\mathfrak n}=\theta\beta\alpha$ is injective. If $r=0$ the rational local ring is $L$ and $J=0$; if $s=0$ then $I=0$; if $C=0$ there is no maximal ideal containing $I=A$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof, continuous differential formula; residue-fibre factorization supplied by Steps 2–6.

lean.statement: theorem affinoid_residual_conormal_injective (K : Type u) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] (r s : ℕ) (f : Fin s → ↥(IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (1 : Fin r → ℝ))) (I : Ideal ↥(IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (1 : Fin r → ℝ))) (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (hgeom : ∀ (L : Type (max u v)) [NormedField L] [IsUltrametricDist L] [CompleteSpace L] (φ : K →+* L), Isometry φ → IsRegularRing (↥(IsRestricted.subring (R := L) (1 : Fin r → ℝ)) ⧸ Ideal.span {g : ↥(IsRestricted.subring (R := L) (1 : Fin r → ℝ)) | ∃ j : Fin s, g.val = MvPowerSeries.map φ (f j).val})) (n : Ideal ↥(IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (1 : Fin r → ℝ))) [n.IsMaximal] (hIn : I ≤ n) : ∃ d : (I ⧸ (n • ⊤ : Submodule ↥(IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (1 : Fin r → ℝ)) I)) →ₗ[ ↥(IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (1 : Fin r → ℝ)) ⧸ n] (Fin r → ↥(IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (1 : Fin r → ℝ)) ⧸ n), (∀ (g : I) (i : Fin r), ∃ dg : ↥(IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (1 : Fin r → ℝ)), dg.val = MvPowerSeries.pderiv K i g.val.val ∧ d (Submodule.Quotient.mk g) i = Ideal.Quotient.mk n dg) ∧ Function.Injective d
